Our Founder

Lindora Kolu Howard-Diawara is a Liberian peace activist and women’s rights advocate. Since founding B4P CODEFOUND in 2015, her leadership has been instrumental in creating sustainable pathways for the next generation of African leaders.

Her work bridges the gap between grassroots activism and global policy, ensuring that the stories and needs of local communities reach international stages like the Commission on the Status of Women. She has dedicated her career to the belief that empowered women are the foundation of a productive nation.

Through mentorship and leadership skill-building, she continues to advocate for a more inclusive and peaceful future across the continent.

Read Executive Message →

Lindora Kolu Howard-Diawara

Founder & Executive Director

Our Core Values

Our values shape every program, partnership, and community initiative, empowering women, uplifting youth, and creating sustainable impact across African communities.

Core Value 01

Respect for Human Rights & Dignity

We uphold the dignity of every individual and promote equality, justice, inclusion, and respect for all people regardless of background.

Core Value 02

People & Communities

We strengthen communities through collaboration, partnerships, innovation, participation, and inclusive development initiatives.

Core Value 03

Passion & Teamwork

We believe sustainable impact is built through teamwork, dedication, leadership, passion, and empowering young people.

Core Value 04

Diversity & Inclusion

We celebrate diversity and create inclusive spaces that encourage participation, trust-building, and equal opportunities for everyone.

Core Value 05

Integrity & Commitment

We remain transparent, dependable, and committed to building sustainable systems and partnerships that advance peace, development, and human security.

Future Investment Initiatives

Capacity Building Fund

Institutional Support: As important it is for individuals and groups to be supported in doing their work, the health and survival of all organizations benefiting from the Foundation’s program will be prioritized. This we believe will help foster accountability, transparency and community participation

Community Business Investment

Community Development: These grants will be expected to serve as a catalyst for jump starting and scaling up specific community led peace and development initiatives.

Our Framework for Impact

Theory of Change

“

The more empowered women and girls become, and the more moral, technical, and financial support they receive, the better the conditions for them and their families. As the conditions of families improve, the more productive and proactive their communities will become. As the conditions of their communities improve, the more productive and proactive the country will become.

01

Empowered Individuals

Providing moral, technical, and financial support to women and girls to build a foundation of leadership.

02

Stronger Families

Transformed individuals improve the conditions of the household, fostering proactive and healthy family units.

03

Proactive Communities

Strong families collaborate to drive collective growth, safety, and prosperity within their local communities.

04

A Productive Nation

A flourishing country built on the productivity and stability of its empowered regions and citizens.

title: About Us
content:
WELCOME TO B4P CODEFOUND

Empowering young minds through education, technology, leadership, and innovation — building a generation ready to transform communities and shape the future of Liberia and beyond.

Our Mission

B4P CODEFOUND — Mission Block

Mission

B4P CODEFOUND seeks to increase and sustain the voice and agency of women and girls by building their capacities to access resources and tools for social justice, cohesion, and financial independence.

Our Goal

B4P CODEFOUND — Goal Block

Goal

Facilitate, accompany, and support community cooperation; enhance local community capacities for promoting and sustaining local peace initiatives, collective and co-created enterprises for poverty reduction, as well as development and shared prosperity.

Our Purpose

B4P CODEFOUND — Purpose Block

Purpose

Our purpose is to inspire, equip, and support young people to discover their identity, unlock their potential, and pursue meaningful paths that impact their lives and communities. Through education, empowerment, and innovation, we guide youth toward clarity, confidence, and purpose-driven leadership.

B4P CODEFOUND Vision

B4P CODEFOUND — Vision Block

Vision

We envisage a world where women and girls lead by creating and promoting entrepreneurial models to foster economic freedom, sustainable peace, and development beyond borders.

IGNITING MINDS, EMPOWERING FUTURES

At B4P CODEFOUND, we nurture innovation, leadership, and digital skills for young women, girls, and communities — shaping the next generation of changemakers in Liberia and beyond.

Explore Our Programs

Explore more of our Focus Here

Empowering Women in Technology

We create opportunities for women and girls to excel in digital skills and tech leadership across Liberia.

Transforming Agriculture

Supporting sustainable agriculture and smart farming solutions to improve livelihoods in communities.

Quality Education for All

Providing educational programs and mentorship to equip the next generation with knowledge and skills.

Health & Wellbeing

We champion health awareness and access to healthcare services for women, girls, and communities.

Community Leadership

Building leadership programs that empower local changemakers to drive positive social impact.

Innovation & Entrepreneurship

Encouraging creativity and entrepreneurship to foster sustainable development and economic growth.

title: Donor Dashboard
About
content:
FAQ

FAQ

General Question

Why do you work both on Peace Building and Economic Development?

Answer: There are two main reasons why we have set out to work on both pillars. Firstly, it is because women and girls living in the context of conflict, post conflict or so-called peace and development are confronted with the issues of conflicts on a daily basis. In order to build and maintain healthy relationships and help others do the same, we believe that creating spaces for learning and sharing of techniques for dealing with issues of conflicts and violence prepares them for a more strategic approach to community building processes. Secondly, having strong economic foundations, being financially independent and less dependance on their male counterparts will enable them lead with confidence and much more determination.     

What is your business and why the choice?

Answer: As a nonprofit, we will grow to become a social enterprise for the sole purpose ensuring that the organization remain less dependent on grants on donors and prepare to sustain its work from the onset. This will require much more creativity in our approach. Success in this direction will be determined by the role and contributions of all partners, targets and or beneficiaries.

With women and girls being targeted to lead key initiatives, how are men and boys expected to participate or benefit?

Answer: Gender equality is at the heart of what we do. As such, we also recognize that the work of women and girls cannot be sustained without the support of men and boys who need to firstly understand that women and girls have rights and that they have much more to offer in helping societies thrive. Through our work, we will identify opportunities and create spaces for learning and collaboration between men, women, boys and girls to help build relationships for peace and development.

Who are your core funders and what thematic areas do they fund?

Answer: Individuals that believe in our potential and work have been very generous over the years. However, we have had some partners (Listed on the home page) that have also been very supportive. We have received both financial, technical and moral support from everyone and for that we are grateful.

How do you bridge intergenerational gaps?

Answer: Our main approach will be through dialogues. Initiatives will be contextualized and each community or group will have the opportunity to determine the engagement and learning path.

How can others get Involved?

Answer: As should on the home page, anyone can join us or support our work. You could join our team by applying for open positions or letting us know ahead of time of you interest. Other options include (1) Volunteering from time to time (2) Support our work by donating (3) Becoming a member of Friends for B4P CODEFOUND and (4) Becoming a partner to collaborate on specific projects, programs and or initiatives.

— Mother Yartu Mama Tokpa, Community Peace Activist, Liberia

Our Strategic Economic Development Models:

Provide capacity building, mentoring and coaching services to women and girls to increase their drive for business development and incubation.

Organize financial planning sessions that will enhance individual and group financial management skills and influence behavioral changes.

Collaborate with strategic partners to provide access to affordable and adaptable financing services, markets, information, and networks.

Organize and facilitate community as well as B2B (Business to Business) exchanges and initiatives that will increase learning and help build trust, confidence as well as foster social venturing and investments.

Establish community level women business development and service centers to provide support for those in need and enhance the knowledge and skills building process of individuals as well as the development and growth of new and existing businesses.

title: Peacebuilding Program
content:
Peacebuilding Program

Peacebuilding & Community Reconciliation

Building Peace.
Strengthening Communities.
Restoring Hope.

Our goal is cultivating harmony, reducing conflict, and building lasting trust across diverse, conflict, and post-conflict communities through dialogue, inclusion, leadership, reconciliation, and sustainable peacebuilding initiatives.

The force and strength for peace will come from people. And, that will happen when people start to realize that all the diversity and differences we see of nationalities, of religions, of cultures, of languages are all beautiful diversities, for they are only on the surface. And, deep down we share the same humanity, the global humanity.

— Satish Kumar
Peacebuilding Objectives

Objectives To:

Educate individuals, communities, and create safe spaces for dialogue, peace education, and information dissemination to help reduce prejudice, stereotypes, and community tensions.

Enhance knowledge and skills of individuals and groups to enable them to play leadership roles in the management, resolution, prevention, and transformation of violence within communities.

Develop a strong network of women and girls’ peace practitioners to facilitate community-level peacebuilding processes, reconciliation, advocacy, and sustainable engagement.

Sustainable Impact

Creating Stronger Communities Through Peace & Unity

Our peacebuilding initiatives are designed to strengthen community cohesion, rebuild trust, encourage reconciliation, and promote sustainable peace across diverse, conflict, and post-conflict communities.

01

Enhanced Community Cohesion, Trust & Sustainable Peace Initiatives

Through dialogue, collaboration, inclusion, and grassroots engagement, communities are empowered to resolve conflicts peacefully, strengthen social bonds, and build lasting systems that promote harmony and resilience.

title: The Director’s Corner
content:
Director's Corner

A leadership space for vision, strategy & reflection.

Official messages and strategic insights from the Office of the Executive Director.

This portal anchors the intellectual foundation of B4P CODEFOUND. It is here that we translate our mission into actionable strategy—elevating the voices of women, girls, and youth while shaping sustainable development throughout Liberia and the global diaspora.
Leadership reflections updated periodically.
Lindora Howard-Diawara
Founder & Executive Director
“Director’s Corner is a reflective space where we share the lessons and strategies shaping our work across Liberia and the diaspora.”
Founder’s Story

Resistance, Resilience, and Resoluteness

A renowned women’s rights campaigner and social justice activist, our founder and executive director, Lindora Kolu Howard-Diawara, understands what it means and how it feels to be a woman searching for survival in a postwar setting.

Lindora experienced severe adversity as a child, including surviving a raging civil war that engulfed her homeland, Liberia, when she was only 12 years old. She began working for peace at 21, unceasingly advocating for equality while pushing for social cohesion across communities and cultures.

With more than 15 years of professional experience, she has helped facilitate and build the capacities of hundreds of children, students, teachers, and organizations. Her work was pivotal in sustaining the Liberian Women’s Peace Movement the advocacy campaign that helped end the Liberian Civil War.

“She is inspired by real-life stories of determination—those that reflect the shifts individuals make from victimhood to agency and the dignity of the human person.”

Education

M.A. International Peace Studies, University of Notre Dame (USA)

B.A. Sociology, University of Liberia

Fellowships

Senior Chevening Fellow (UK)

US State Dept. IVLP Alum

New American Leadership Academy

Global Impact

World Bank (GPSURR), Mercy Corps (Mali), WANEP, and the Kroc Institute Alumni Network.

SNAPSHOT OF HERSTORY
Leadership Strategy

How the Director guides our core mission.

Beyond programmes, the Director provides the strategic compass that keeps B4P CODEFOUND anchored in women’s rights, youth leadership, and resilient development.

Priority 01

Women’s Leadership & Voice

Championing spaces where women and girls lead institutions and shape national policy across Africa and the diaspora.

Priority 02

Economic Resilience

Linking entrepreneurship and financial literacy to move households from survival to sustainable independence.

Priority 03

Peace & Social Cohesion

Promoting inclusive dialogue and reconciliation to ensure the next generation grows up free from the cycles of violence.

“Every strategy we design must translate into a tangible, positive shift in someone’s dignity and life. We listen deeply to act decisively.”
Lindora Howard-Diawara Founder & Executive Director
  • Ground programmes in community reality.
  • Invest in intergenerational leadership.
  • Ensure ethical resource stewardship.
  • Forge powerful global partnerships.
Director's Strategic Vision

Keeping our impact anchored and people-centered.

Priority 01

Centering Women & Youth

Ensuring that programme design and decision-making keep local voices at the heart of our strategy.

Priority 02

Linking Peace & Prosperity

Treating economic development and social cohesion as interconnected priorities for national growth.

Priority 03

Building Trust & Impact

Strengthening internal reporting so every partner can see the tangible results of our shared resources.

“Our commitment is to stay close to the communities we serve while engaging confidently with global conversations on justice and development.”

Lindora Howard-Diawara Founder & Executive Director, B4P CODEFOUND
Leadership Model Women & Youth-Driven
Approach Evidence-Informed & Community-Led

title: About
content:
WHO WE ARE?

Established 2015 • 501(c)(3) Nonprofit

RE-IMAGINING
EMPOWERMENT

The Business for Peace Community Development Foundation promotes political, social, and economic justice globally. We work with women and girls to foster gender equality and dismantle the vicious circle of violence impacting society.

11+ Years of
Global Impact
01

Build

Build women and girl’s confidence to act as agents of change at local, national, and international levels.

02

Invest

Invest resources in women, girls, and communities to enhance their self-reliance and development.

03

Connect

Connect individuals and groups to foster learning and encourage collective actions that yield greater community impact.

Vision

We envisage a world where women and girls lead by creating and promoting entrepreneurial models to foster economic freedom, sustainable peace, and development beyond borders.

Goal

Facilitate, accompany, and support community cooperation; enhance local community capacities for promoting and sustaining local peace initiatives and shared prosperity.

Mission

B4P CODEFOUND seeks to increase and sustain the voice and agency of women and girls by building their capacities to access resources for social justice and financial independence.

OUR CORE VALUES

Aspire to remain gender and conflict sensitive

Show respect for human and women’s rights

Uphold the dignity of every person

Strategically promote and encourage:

  • Community cooperation
  • Diversity & Inclusion
  • Collaboration for peace and development

Join the movement @B4P-CODEFOUND
